Memory Architecture: Four tiers: working (KV cache) / episodic (Kafka+TimescaleDB) / semantic (Neo4j KG) / procedural (skill library in pgvector); learned memory-controller policy
Reasoning/Planning Loop: ReAct + plan-and-execute; reflection writes lesson nodes into KG so failures are never repeated
Learning/Self-Improvement: Three timescales: in-context retrieval, nightly consolidation into graph+skills, weekly LoRA-DPO on curated traces; base model frozen
Tool Use & Action Execution: Typed function schemas via capability broker; policy gate by risk score; HITL token for irreversible actions; full audit log
World Model/Representation: The KG is the world model: entities, causal edges, belief confidences; validator replays episodes against predictions
Safety/Governance: Built into substrate: policy gate, signed skills, hash-chained append-only logs, separate monitor model, approval queue
Evaluation Strategy: LongMemEval, lesson-reuse tests, WebArena/GAIA/SWE-bench, red-team tool-misuse, 30-day skill-growth cohorts
Persistence/Runtime: K8s microservices; Postgres/Neo4j/TimescaleDB + Kafka; checkpointed working memory for crash resume
Multi-Agent/Orchestration: Shared memory tiers across task agents; librarian (consolidation) + critic (reflection) specialists; stigmergic via event bus
Engineering Feasibility: Medium: memory-controller policy is the hard part; start heuristic. 8xH100-class node per heavy deployment
Non-Obvious Insight: The memory system IS the agent; the LLM is just the read/write head - capability becomes cumulative with frozen weights

Memory Architecture: Partitioned by role: private Qdrant per specialist; shared blackboard (Redis+Postgres); collective semantic memory writeable only by 2-of-3 specialist consensus
Reasoning/Planning Loop: Meta-planner builds subtask DAG; specialists work concurrently; critic quorum (3 diverse models) majority-gates each branch
Learning/Self-Improvement: Individual: versioned prompts A/B tested weekly. Collective: mined collaboration patterns compiled into routing policies; no weight updates
Tool Use & Action Execution: Least-privilege tool belts per specialist; central gateway with rate limits, gVisor/Firecracker sandboxing, quorum for side effects
World Model/Representation: No single model: overlapping partial models per specialist; disagreements surfaced as explicit conflicts for quorum resolution
Safety/Governance: Separation of powers: no agent plans+executes irreversible acts; critics from different families; dumb (non-LLM) policy gateway; supervisor dashboard
Evaluation Strategy: Division-of-labor benchmarks vs single-agent baselines; coordination overhead ratio; compromised-specialist containment tests
Persistence/Runtime: Temporal workflows for durable DAG; stateless workers on K8s; Redis hot + Postgres durable; full event-log replay
Multi-Agent/Orchestration: The architecture: blackboard + typed envelopes + quorum voting; dynamic DAG rewiring; pluggable specialist registry
Engineering Feasibility: Medium: coordination overhead can hit 10x tokens; strict message budgets required. Many parallel cheap-model calls
Non-Obvious Insight: No single point of cognition to compromise: a swarm degrades gracefully where a monolith fails everywhere at once

Memory Architecture: Generative not retrievable: compressed predictive world model + surprise buffer; episodic recall = re-simulation from latent seeds (RocksDB)
Reasoning/Planning Loop: Model-predictive control: sample action sequences, roll out thousands of simulated futures, execute best first action, replan
Learning/Self-Improvement: Continuous: every observation vs prediction -> error gradient updates world model (EWC-regularized); curiosity drive maximizes information gain
Tool Use & Action Execution: Tools as causal interventions with learned forward models; prefer well-modeled tools; halt if reality diverges from simulation
World Model/Representation: Hierarchical latent predictive model (JEPA-style): sensorimotor / event / intentional levels; validated like a weather model
Safety/Governance: Actions only after safe simulated futures; learned harm-prediction head; pessimistic minimax planner for high-stakes; inspectable simulation traces
Evaluation Strategy: Next-event prediction accuracy at horizons; fewer real actions vs reactive baselines; trap-scenario avoidance; calibration diagrams
Persistence/Runtime: Fast loop (planner+GPU) + slow loop (background training); immutable versioned models; planner names model version used
Multi-Agent/Orchestration: Others modeled as world dynamics; federated prediction-error averaging shares learning without central orchestrator
Engineering Feasibility: Hard: open-ended world models are research-grade; start one domain, degrade to reactive where uncertain. Training-heavy GPU
Non-Obvious Insight: Most failures are prediction failures not logic failures; better prediction IS better safety - capability and safety scale together

Memory Architecture: Dual: neural (pgvector fuzzy recall) + symbolic (Datalog fact store); every fact in both forms linked by ID; PDDL operators mirror neural skills
Reasoning/Planning Loop: Generate-and-verify: neural proposes, symbolic verifier (Z3/SMT) checks constraints; solver-first mode for formal domains; unverified outputs flagged
Learning/Self-Improvement: Neural fine-tuning/DPO + symbolic ILP rule induction; distillation bridge: repeated neural successes -> candidate symbolic rules
Tool Use & Action Execution: Tools declare formal contracts (pre/post/effects); symbolic composition proves chain safety; uncontracted tools sandboxed
World Model/Representation: Hybrid: symbolic causal graph (do-calculus counterfactuals) over neural embedding space (analogy); consistency maintainer flags disagreements
Safety/Governance: Safety as proof obligations: critical invariants must be PROVEN before execution; trusted base (verifier) is small, deterministic, ML-free
Evaluation Strategy: ProofWriter/FOLIO, hybrid constraint tasks, verification coverage % (target 100% for irreversible acts), prompt-injection vs verifier tests
Persistence/Runtime: Stateless neural tier + ACID symbolic tier (system of record); versioned snapshots of fact base + adapters for re-verification
Multi-Agent/Orchestration: Intuition agents (neural, propose) vs auditor agents (symbolic, deterministic, verify); mandatory propose-verify pipeline
Engineering Feasibility: Medium: formalization bottleneck - writing correct contracts is labor-intensive; start with highest-risk tools only. CPU-cheap
Non-Obvious Insight: Keep neural maximally free AND symbolic maximally rigid; capability from freedom, safety from refusal to negotiate - separation beats blending

Memory Architecture: No separate store: weights ARE long-term memory; small fast episodic FAISS cache consolidated nightly via continual update then cleared; EWC protects important weights
Reasoning/Planning Loop: Unremarkable ReAct loop by design; traces become training data - planning improves via gradient updates on own history, not cleverer prompts
Learning/Self-Improvement: The architecture: nightly LoRA+EWC on filtered traces, regression-gated (must pass retention+alignment suites or rollback); self-distillation on weak domains; federated gradient sharing
Tool Use & Action Execution: Tool proficiency learned via replay buffer; new tools onboarded through sandboxed tutorial protocol generating permanent training data; trust scores widen permissions
World Model/Representation: Implicit in weights but queryable: periodic model interrogation builds explicit belief snapshots forming a visible trajectory over time
Safety/Governance: Constitutional core (frozen classifier) immune to drift; update provenance with forensic rollback; max 1 update/day; human sign-off on alignment shifts
Evaluation Strategy: Retention (anti-forgetting) as #1 metric; forward transfer; alignment-stability across updates; 90-day human-satisfaction deployments
Persistence/Runtime: Model registry with immutable checkpoints; nightly training pipeline; update ledger: signed log of every batch/hyperparam/eval per version
Multi-Agent/Orchestration: Single-agent by design; federated update exchange (gradients not data, DP-protected) gives species-level learning with privacy
Engineering Feasibility: Hard: stable lifelong learning at LLM scale unproven; regression gate + rollback make failures survivable. 2-3x inference budget for training
Non-Obvious Insight: Starting weights matter less than the update rule: a mediocre model with an excellent learning loop beats a brilliant frozen model

Memory Architecture: Filesystem IS memory: git-backed workspace, MEMORY.md curated by agent, grep/find + incremental embedding index; human-readable and editable
Reasoning/Planning Loop: Observe->think->act in a real shell; plans are PLAN.md files; no separate planner module; scratchpad and workshop are one place
Learning/Self-Improvement: Self-authored LESSONS.md entries; repeated procedures codified as scripts in ~/skills/; human promotes best to shared infra
Tool Use & Action Execution: Full shell (maximalist): file I/O, compilers, browsers, cron; containment layers: VM snapshots, filesystem policy, egress allow-list proxy, confirmation tokens
World Model/Representation: The machine state IS the world model (filesystem, processes, topology); external world probed and recorded as annotated markdown beliefs
Safety/Governance: Containment-first: VM boundary primary; append-only command audit log (agent cannot modify); per-session capability tokens for high-impact acts
Evaluation Strategy: SWE-bench/GAIA/OSWorld; multi-session persistence-after-reboot tests; containment red-teaming; agent-authored skill count after 30 days
Persistence/Runtime: A VM with files: sessions are shell sessions; backup is rsync; cron gives temporal persistence; replicate by copying a directory
Multi-Agent/Orchestration: Subagents are scoped shell sessions with task files; parent monitors via filesystem; lockfiles for mutual exclusion
Engineering Feasibility: Easiest: everything exists today; only research part is agent file discipline. Minimal compute: one VM + inference
Non-Obvious Insight: Unix already solved agency (files, pipes, processes, cron, logs); AGI needs a model trained to live in the 50-year-old runtime, not a new runtime

Memory Architecture: Compartmented by classification (public/internal/confidential/restricted); tags at write time; Postgres row-level security enforces need-to-know at DB level; full access audit
Reasoning/Planning Loop: Dual-loop: propose -> MANDATORY governance review -> execute -> attest; harness enforces review, planner cannot skip; fast table lookup vs deliberative by risk
Learning/Self-Improvement: Gated: improvement proposals need alignment impact assessment; canary cohorts (1%) with 7-day no-regression requirement; self-modification = highest privilege
Tool Use & Action Execution: Object-capability security: no ambient authority; capabilities granted per session with budgets; mid-task escalation needs re-authorization; forensic attribution
World Model/Representation: Normative + descriptive: policy graph of obligations/permissions/prohibitions (human-authored, versioned); conflicts always resolve for normative
Safety/Governance: Governance IS the architecture: compartments, checkpoints, capabilities, normative model, canary gating, hash-chained audit, human override APIs
Evaluation Strategy: 10k adversarial compliance scenarios (target 100%); governance overhead <15% for low-risk; red-team the governance; operator override usage
Persistence/Runtime: Policy-enforcing runtime/harness mediating every state change; compartmented Postgres; WORM audit log; minimal audited harness
Multi-Agent/Orchestration: Chain of command: principal delegates attenuated sub-capabilities; every delegation logged; no unsupervised agents possible
Engineering Feasibility: Medium: risk is usability - heavy governance invites bypass; risk-proportional friction; governance adds small-model review cost
Non-Obvious Insight: Derive capability architecture FROM governance constraints (max power inside safety envelope) instead of patching safety onto capability

Memory Architecture: One unified vector index (FAISS/Qdrant) for everything; hybrid dense+BM25 + reranker; TTL expiry; no tiers/graphs/splits - retrieval over a big pile
Reasoning/Planning Loop: Model + tight loop + two augmentations: self-consistency sampling on hard calls, fixed scratchpad token budget; planning emerges from training
Learning/Self-Improvement: None by design: improvement = provider releases better base model (swap checkpoint) + growing retrieval corpus; total behavior predictability
Tool Use & Action Execution: Single flat function-calling interface; tools documented as retrievable chunks; blunt denylist + human approval for irreversible actions
World Model/Representation: None, explicitly: pre-trained weights + corpus are the knowledge; explicit world models judged premature until proven better
Safety/Governance: Thin: moderation APIs, tool denylist, approval list, full logging; safety via epistemic humility - fewer modules, predictable failures
Evaluation Strategy: Head-to-head vs complex architectures (null hypothesis: Occam matches); ablation discipline per addition; run-to-run variance
Persistence/Runtime: One inference server + one vector DB + logs; single Docker Compose; snapshot backups; horizontal scaling = more replicas
Multi-Agent/Orchestration: None: one model one loop; parallelism via tools not agents; multi-agent treated as prompting pattern not primitive
Engineering Feasibility: Easiest: days to build off-the-shelf; risk is the ceiling - bounded by base model, no mechanism to exceed it
Non-Obvious Insight: Most agent architectures are never ablated vs the trivial baseline; Occam IS the maintained control group keeping every other design honest
